P1 S2: the stock box and your own stock, built

Built and checked; waiting for your approval to merge. On the Machining step a see-through stock box shows around a milled part. A Stock button beside the view buttons turns it on or off. Under Stock, Your stock takes three sizes in inches. Apply puts the removal on your block and adds one facing line per axis. All of it is as the approved mock-up shows (D-089).

Try it: open the demo, tap clean_pocket.step (first in the list), then Machining. Tap Stock to turn the box off and on. Type 3.25, 2.25 and 1.125, then tap Apply. Pull request.

What you'll see

Against the mock-up, the numbers, wording and placement are the same. The only difference is the mock-up's light tint, which marked the new rows on that page and is not part of the app.

What was checked

  • npm run check: exit 0 in 601 s (budget 900 s): 876 unit tests, 119 browser tests and 6 timed browser tests passed. Parity quick: 122 of 122 files the same on the existing key (117 s).
  • New tests, each seen failing first, plus two planted bugs caught: "ghost stock" (the button, on and off, hidden in the Machine view and on other steps, the box's size and centre, the box back after a PDF export), and "typed stock" (the mock-up's numbers, the box at your size, typed text kept when the list redraws, too small, a bad size, Enter, and a new part clears it). Unit tests: "facing per side" (the spec's 4 × 2.5 × 1.25 in on a 3.937 × 2.362 × 1.181 in part: 0.0315, 0.0690 and 0.0345 in per side), the pairing on a part turned in its frame, "stock too small" and "bad stock size".
  • Parity passes on the existing key, so the engine is unchanged (J7).

Small choices made while building (say if any should change)

  • The part's sides are taken as the Stock line shows them (to 0.001 in), so typing the size shown is accepted with 0 facing. The spec's example numbers come out this way.
  • If more than one size is too small, there is one sentence per size.
  • After a wrong Apply, the size in use stays: the box and lines don't change.
  • The box hides with its button in the Machine view and on other steps. It is not in the PDF picture.
  • A turned part has no box, no button and no Your stock.
  • Your stock stays when you change material or process on the same part, and goes when you open another part (D-089).
